backfill_note: This scaffold benchmark was run on 2026-06-18; the two throwaway project trees under tmp/vite-bench/ were deleted per the finite-disk policy. run.sh + fixture/gen-app.mjs are reconstructed from the recorded methodology so a third party can rebuild the identical 24-component app on both Vite versions and re-measure. results.json holds the numbers measured on 2026-06-18 — build ratios are stable, but absolute ms are machine-dependent and will drift.

environment.note: Absolute build times are machine-dependent; the RATIO (Vite 8 build vs Vite 7 build) is the portable signal, not absolute ms. This is a scaffold bench (a freshly generated representative app), NOT a production-app migration.

subject.name: vite
subject.install: npm i vite@8.0.16 @vitejs/plugin-react@6.0.2 into a clean project
subject.note: Vite 8 makes Rolldown the default bundler for both dev pre-bundling and production build; direct deps drop esbuild and rollup in favor of `rolldown@1.0.3`.

baseline.name: vite
baseline.install: npm i vite@7.3.5 @vitejs/plugin-react@5 into an identical project
baseline.invocation: same source tree, only the vite + plugin-react versions differ

data_source.name: npm registry
data_source.drift_warning: Dependency facts (rolldown@1.0.3 as vite@8.0.16's direct dep; esbuild/rollup removed; @vitejs/plugin-react@6.0.2 peer vite ^8.0.0) are pinned to exact versions and were re-confirmed stable on 2026-08-16. Package COUNTS (107 vs 62) and native-binary sizes reflect those exact pins on win-x64; a different platform or newer patch releases can shift the counts. Pins do not drift; `latest` would.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: discarded at run time (finite local disk)
